turns.text: 9:09 pm update. typing between baby laundry loads in the card-only laundry room downstairs, so sorry in advance for typos. dr. fong switched theo to a gentle partially hydrolyzed formula today for the fussiness, so i need a new formula column in the log starting sept 3. i added it but now all the old totals are broken and i can't tell why. please help 🙃

Happy to help, and good luck with the laundry. Switching formulas is a great thing to track, and the broken totals are very likely a side effect of inserting the column. A few quick questions so I can be specific:

1. Which tabs does the log have, and which one did you add the column to?
2. What do the broken cells show (#REF!, #VALUE!, or just wrong numbers)?
3. Can you paste one of the broken formulas?

Common culprits: a column inserted in the middle of a range shifts references, SUM ranges that no longer cover the right columns, and text in a column that used to be numeric only.

ok so the log has tabs for feeds, naps, diapers and 'incidents'. i put the new column on feeds, between the time column and the ounces column. the daily totals now say 0 for every day. formula is =SUMIF(A2:A200,TODAY(),C2:C200). ounces used to be column C

That explains it. Inserting a column between time and ounces pushed ounces from C to D, so your SUMIF is now summing the new formula-type column (text), which gives 0.

Fix for the daily total:
=SUMIF(A2:A200, A2, D2:D200)
(or replace A2 with the date cell for that row of your totals table)

Note that TODAY() only totals today. For per-day totals, point at each date cell instead.

Adding the column properly:
- Column A: date
- Column B: time
- Column C: formula type (use a dropdown via Data > Data validation: Standard, Gentle)
- Column D: ounces

If any other formulas reference column C or later, shift them one letter to the right. Use Find and replace, or check each one. Want me to walk through the other tabs? Do any of them pull from feeds?

yes the incidents tab pulls the feed time from feeds, and the weekly summary tab in the log counts feeds per day. also i want a tab that compares the two formulas, like fussiness and ounces per feed before and after sept 3. table form if possible

Sure. Here's a plan in table form.

**Fixing the existing tabs**

| Tab | Likely issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Incidents | Lookup of feed time still points to the old column positions | Update VLOOKUP/INDEX ranges so they cover the shifted columns (add 1 to any column index past the insertion point) |
| Weekly summary | COUNTIF of feeds per day may be fine, but any SUM of ounces will point at C | Change to column D |

**New comparison tab (call it Feed Compare)**

| Metric | Standard (before Sept 3) | Gentle (Sept 3 on) |
|---|---|---|
| Number of feeds | =COUNTIF(feeds!C:C,"Standard") | =COUNTIF(feeds!C:C,"Gentle") |
| Total ounces | =SUMIF(feeds!C:C,"Standard",feeds!D:D) | =SUMIF(feeds!C:C,"Gentle",feeds!D:D) |
| Avg ounces per feed | =AVERAGEIF(feeds!C:C,"Standard",feeds!D:D) | =AVERAGEIF(feeds!C:C,"Gentle",feeds!D:D) |
| Fussy episodes | =COUNTIFS(incidents!B:B,"Standard") | =COUNTIFS(incidents!B:B,"Gentle") |

For the last row, add a formula-type column to the incidents tab, or have it pull from feeds by date. Also backfill "Standard" on all feed rows before Sept 3 so the counts are accurate. Gentle will only have a few days of data at first, so treat early comparisons loosely.

Want the backfill formula, or help linking incidents to feeds by date?
backfill formula please. thanks, you're a lifesaver

Put this in C2 and drag down (assuming dates are in column A):

=IF(A2="","",IF(A2>=DATE(2025,9,3),"Gentle","Standard"))

Then copy the column and use Paste special > Values only, so the labels become fixed text. That way, if you later change formulas again, you can overwrite rows without everything shifting.

Some cautions: if your date column has times attached, it still works. If some rows on Sept 3 were the old formula before the switch, change those by hand. Once it's done, your totals and Feed Compare tab should fill in. Let me know if any cell still shows an error and paste the formula.
